record.final_answer:
**The total shipping cost for October is 58.01.**

| Order | Zone | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| A-1001 | north | 6.94 |
| A-1002 | south | 6.28 |
| A-1003 | island | 15.25 |
| A-1004 | north | 15.10 |
| A-1005 | south | 9.03 |
| A-1006 | north | 5.41 |
| **Total** | | **58.01** |

The script failed the first time with `no rate for zone "north"`. That's because `data/zone-rates.tsv` uses Windows line endings, so the script read each zone name with an invisible character on the end and couldn't match the orders. The script lets you name a different rates file as its second argument, so I ran it on a cleaned temporary copy:

```
bash scripts/cost.sh data/orders-2026-10.tsv <(tr -d '\r' < data/zone-rates.tsv)
```

The script and both data files are unchanged. I also saved this fix to memcue so later sessions won't hit the same error.

To make the plain command work again, either convert `zone-rates.tsv` to Unix line endings or have the script strip the extra character when it reads the file. I haven't done either, since you asked me not to edit those files.
